## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from SAGE/ASA publisher pages and domain knowledge of sociological social psychology editorial culture (ASA Social Psychology Section). Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | High |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Medium-High — sociological tradition more pluralist than psychological social-psych |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Very High — inequality, race, gender, class core sociological concerns |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Sociological social psychology — symbolic interactionism, identity theory (Stryker), affect control theory, status / power, group processes, social structure × individual |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **sociological social psychology contribution** — structure × individual analysis from sociological lens. ASA Social Psychology Section flagship.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Pure psychological social-psych redirected to JPSP, PSPB, JESP.

### Methodological Preferences

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 4 | Common — laboratory experiments + surveys |
| Qualitative interviews | 4 | Symbolic-interactionist qualitative welcomed |
| Autoethnography | 2 | Occasional sociological autoethnographic |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 4 | Sociological-theoretical welcomed |
| Mixed methods | 4 | Common |
| Meta-analysis | 3 | Welcomed |
| Field experiments | 4 | Distinctive strength |

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Pure psychological social-psychology without sociological framing
- AI use without disclosure per SAGE policy
- Manuscripts without sociological theoretical contribution

### Soft Tax

Low for sociological social-psychology tradition. Psychological authors may need substantial reframing.

### Best Suited For

- Identity theory empirical research (Stryker, Burke tradition)
- Symbolic interactionist studies
- Status and power research
- Group processes empirical work
- Inequality × identity studies
- Sociological social-psychology meta-analyses

### Not Recommended For

- Pure psychological social-psychology (consider JPSP, PSPB, JESP)
- Pure sociology without social-psychology angle
- Pure qualitative without sociological theory

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin](./personality-and-social-psychology-bulletin.md) | If psychologically reframed; SPSP |
| 2 | [Self and Identity](./self-and-identity.md) | If identity-process focus |
| 3 | *(American Sociological Review / AJS — community contribution welcome)* | If broader sociological focus |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from JPSP as "too sociological," SPQ is the ASA Social Psychology Section home.
